follow-up time: 6 hours (5 hours before and 1 hour after onset of fever)
cohort: 100 term pregnant women who developed fever and had an intrauterine pressure catheter
finding: A decline in uterine contractility occurs 2 hours after the onset of maternal fever in the setting of chorioamnionitis, which may contribute to an increased risk of cesarean delivery and postpartum hemorrhage.
mod_finding: A decline in uterine contractility occurs 2 hours after the onset of maternal fever, which is associated with an increased risk of cesarean delivery.
